hints: Look closely at diagrams 1 and 2. One shows single C-C links, the other shows a C=C link. Which one means extra hydrogens are missing?
Remember that saturated means full of hydrogen with no C=C, while unsaturated means at least one C=C. Both types are still fatty acids, so both must have the acid end.
walkthrough:
**Decode what 1, 2 and 3 show**

Look at the drawings one by one. Diagram 1 is a C-C single bond in the hydrocarbon chain. Diagram 2 is a C=C double bond in the chain. Diagram 3 is the carboxyl group (-COOH) at the end.

All fatty acids have a chain plus an acid end, so 3 is always present.

**Recall saturated vs unsaturated**

A saturated fatty acid is saturated with hydrogen. It has only single bonds between carbons, so no C=C.

An unsaturated fatty acid has at least one C=C double bond, which creates a kink. It still has many single bonds elsewhere in the chain.

**Match to the table**

Unsaturated needs 1 (single) + 2 (double) + 3 (acid end). Saturated needs 1 (single) + 3 (acid end) only, with no 2.

That combination is row A.

options.A: Correct. Unsaturated has single bonds, at least one double bond, and the carboxyl group (1, 2 and 3). Saturated has only single bonds plus the carboxyl group (1 and 3 only).
options.B: Not correct. A saturated fatty acid cannot contain bond 2, because bond 2 is a C=C double bond which would make it unsaturated.
options.C: Not correct. This is back to front. It gives the unsaturated acid no double bond and the saturated acid a double bond.
options.D: Not correct. An unsaturated acid must also contain many single bonds (1), not only double bonds, and a saturated acid must not contain a double bond (2).
